attacks.claim: The owner's rule of 15 November 2026: where the readings differ on a forfeiture's last day, the record must not block on the earlier reading; keep the held reading in `counting`, list every other defensible counting in `otherCountings`, and make the message name each reading and its source, including whether CPCA 405 applies to the deadline of Law 90-04 and of CPCA 504.
attacks.verifierQuote: [cpca 504 ¶1] يجب رفع الدعوى أمام القسم الاجتماعي في أجل لا يتجاوز ستة (6) أشهر من تاريخ تسليم محضر عدم الصلح، وذلك تحت طائلة سقوط الحق في رفع الدعوى. [cpca 405 ¶1] تحسب كل الآجال المنصوص عليها في هذا القانون كاملة، ولا يحسب يوم التبليغ أو التبليغ الرسمي ويوم انقضاء الأجل. [cpca 405 ¶4] إذا كان اليوم الأخير من الأجل ليس يوم عمل كليا أو جزئيا، يمدد الأجل إلى أول يوم عمل موالي. [labour-disputes 36 ¶1] في حالة عدم المصالحة، يرفع الطرف الذي له مصلحة دعوى أمام المحكمة الفاصلة في المسائل الاجتماعية.
attacks.quoteRef: cpca 504 ¶1; cpca 405 ¶1, ¶3, ¶4 (law-08-09 wording, store); labour-disputes 36 ¶1 (law-90-04 wording, store); law 91-28 art. 1, Official Journal 1991 no. 68, p. 2654
attacks.change: The texts allow two countings of the six months of cpca 504, so the record changes. 405 applies to 504 on its words (504 is a period 'المنصوص عليها في هذا القانون'), so the extension of ¶4 applies under every reading; Law 90-04 sets no filing period of its own (36 ¶1 names none; the store holds articles 1 to 40 in the 90-04 wording, and the ledger does not cover that law; its amendment by law 91-28, read on the Official Journal 1991 no. 68, p. 2654, file A1991068.pdf, SHA-256 f9d1dc6a42e87bed52b98ca99aeda954b40dad75dc4ed83435dc00bbec72c327, touches only art. 40 ¶2: 'يمدد الأجل المحدد في الفقرة الثانية من المادة 40 ... الى غاية 30 يونيو سنة 1992'; no later amendment was searched), so the record has no 90-04 deadline to count. What differs is the first day (open point o4): 405 ¶1 leaves out 'يوم التبليغ أو التبليغ الرسمي', while 504 runs from 'تسليم' the record. d5 and d9 keep as `counting` the reading the record held (excludeFirstAndLastDay, extended; b32 to b35), which is also the later last day, and now list in `otherCountings` the reading that the day of delivery counts (excludeFirstDay, extended; b37, b32, b34, b35), one day earlier. The block of d5 therefore already falls only after the latest last day and its band; nothing in its condition or effect changes. Both messages now name the two readings with their sources, say that 405 governs 504 and that Law 90-04 (art. 36) sets no other period, and d5's message says the export is blocked only after the later last day and its band. o4: refs add d9, its second reading cites b32 too, its note says which reading sits where. d2 (a limitation that one reading treats as a forfeiture, o3): it only warns under every reading, so the block rule does not touch it; its other defensible counting, extension to the next working day (o16: cpca 405 ¶3 and ¶4 against civil-code 314 ¶1 and 405 ¶1 'في هذا القانون'), is now listed in `otherCountings` (b11, b34, b35) and named with its source in the message. d1, d3, d4, d6, d7, d8 are limitations that only warn; their counting readings stay in o15 and o16 and their messages, unchanged. Worked examples ex55 (petition on the held last day, one day late on the other reading: d5 warns), ex56 (past the later last day and its band: d5 blocks) and ex57 (d2's last day on a Friday, petition on the Sunday: warns).
